deities: Surya (as Burhadita/Vriddhaditya, the old Sun God)

history.period: 9th century CE (some architectural analysis suggests 13th century - verify)
history.summary: Ancient Sun temple at Katarmal village, about 17 km from Almora, at ~2,116 m. Built in the 9th century by Katyuri king Katarmalla; dedicated to Surya as Burhadita/Vriddhaditya. Called the second most important Sun temple in India after Konark. East-facing main shrine surrounded by 44-45 subsidiary shrines (Shiva-Parvati, Lakshmi-Narayana); fine carved wooden doors were moved to the National Museum, Delhi after theft of the original deity. Designated a monument of national importance. PERIOD NOTE: one architectural analysis places it around the 13th century (verify). No documented annual festival found in sources (flagged). CSV town/state correction: CSV says 'Almora Cantonment'; actual town is Almora, and the state is Uttarakhand.

name: Katarmal Sun Temple
town_description: Almora is a historic hill town in Kumaon, Uttarakhand, perched on a ridge of the Kumaon Hills at about 1,638 m. A former Chand-dynasty capital, it is known for its temples, bazaars, and panoramic Himalayan views.

travel.road: Motorable road to Kosi (nearest town, ~1.5 km from temple); final ~2 km is a foot trek through villages

visitor_information.best_time: May to September ideal per travel guides; monsoon (heavy rains) should be avoided
